question: What is the primary purpose of performing a gastric lavage on a patient?

options.A: To measure daily digestive enzyme production in the pancreas
options.B: To provide long-term nutritional support for unconscious patients
options.C: To relieve chronic constipation by clearing the lower bowels
options.D: To remove ingested poisons from the stomach before they are absorbed

explanation: Gastric lavage acts as an emergency washing technique specifically targeted at flushing out harmful substances from the upper gastrointestinal tract before systemic absorption takes place. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T12#GNS212_U1_T12_h1)

question: Why is the timing of gastric lavage crucial after a toxic ingestion?

options.A: Nurse fatigue prevents safe tube insertion after the first hour
options.B: Substances leave the stomach quickly and enter the intestines within hours
options.C: The stomach lining becomes permanently closed off after two hours
options.D: Lavage fluid reacts dangerously with most drugs if delayed too long

explanation: Once toxins pass through the pylorus into the small intestine, washing out the stomach no longer retrieves the substance because absorption happens rapidly in the intestines. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T12#GNS212_U1_T12_h1)

question: Which of the following is an absolute contraindication for gastric lavage?

options.A: Consuming a small amount of liquid plant fertilizer
options.B: Ingestion of strong corrosive alkali acids
options.C: A mild overdose of over-the-counter paracetamol
options.D: Swallowing a non-toxic household plastic toy

explanation: Corrosive substances severely damage tissue, meaning the mechanical friction of a lavage tube can easily cause an esophageal or gastric perforation. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T12#GNS212_U1_T12_h2)

question: A patient arrives in the emergency ward after drinking kerosene. What is the main danger if a nurse performs gastric lavage?

options.B: Chemical pneumonia from aspiration into the lungs
options.C: Complete blockage of the large intestine
options.D: Severe permanent staining of the tooth enamel

explanation: Hydrocarbons have very low viscosity and easily slip into the respiratory tract during lavage, causing severe, life-threatening lung inflammation. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T12#GNS212_U1_T12_h2)

question: Why is a large-bore tube used for gastric lavage instead of a standard small feeding tube?

options.A: To make it easier for the nurse to push fluid deep into the small intestines
options.B: To ensure the fluid goes directly into the respiratory airway for safety
options.C: To allow pill fragments and food pieces to pass out without blocking the tube
options.D: To prevent the patient from experiencing any gag reflex during insertion

explanation: Small tubes easily clog with partially digested food or pill debris, rendering the wash ineffective; large-bore tubes provide a clear channel for thick debris to escape. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T12#GNS212_U1_T12_h3)

question: What is the primary reason for keeping a functioning suction apparatus nearby during a gastric lavage setup?

options.A: To suck out blood from the esophagus before the tube goes in
options.B: To clear the airway immediately if the patient vomits or aspirates
options.C: To pump air into the stomach and inflate it for better viewing
options.D: To clean the outside of the rubber tube after the procedure ends

explanation: Vomiting is a common reflex during lavage, and immediate suction is critical to keep the airway clear and prevent aspiration pneumonia. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T12#GNS212_U1_T12_h3)

question: Why must an endotracheal tube with an inflated cuff be placed in an unconscious patient before gastric lavage?

options.A: To keep the patient's mouth open wide during tube insertion
options.B: To measure the exact temperature of the lavage fluid
options.C: To deliver extra oxygen straight to the stomach lining
options.D: To protect the airway and stop fluid from entering the lungs

explanation: Unconscious patients lose their protective swallowing and gag reflexes, so a cuffed airway tube creates a physical barrier against aspiration of stomach washings. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T12#GNS212_U1_T12_h4)

question: What baseline assessment is most critical to perform and record before starting a gastric lavage?

options.A: Abdominal skin turgor and color tone
options.B: Recent dietary history for the past week

explanation: Recording baseline vitals and mental status allows the nurse to monitor for rapid changes caused by toxin absorption or procedural complications like vagal stimulation. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T12#GNS212_U1_T12_h4)

question: In which position should a patient be placed during a gastric lavage to reduce safety risks?

options.A: Left lateral position with the head lowered slightly
options.B: Flat on the back with legs raised high in the air
options.C: Sitting completely upright straight in a hard chair
options.D: Right lateral position with the head elevated high

explanation: The left lateral Trendelenburg position keeps the stomach contents pooled away from the pylorus and promotes safe drainage away from the airway. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T12#GNS212_U1_T12_h5)

question: When should the nurse stop the repeating cycles of fluid instillation and drainage during a gastric lavage?

options.A: When the collection bucket is half filled with fluid
options.B: When exactly one hour has passed on the clock
options.C: When the returned lavage fluid runs completely clear
options.D: When the patient asks for a glass of cold water

explanation: The wash cycles continue until the fluid coming back out is completely clear of toxins, pills, or debris, indicating the stomach is empty. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T12#GNS212_U1_T12_h5)

question: Why is activated charcoal often instilled right before the lavage tube is removed?

options.A: To lubricate the tube so it slips out of the throat without friction
options.B: To stimulate normal bowel movements and speed up total digestion
options.C: To neutralize any acidic cleaning fluids remaining in the stomach wall
options.D: To catch and bind any remaining toxin particles left behind in the gut

explanation: Charcoal binds tightly to residual toxins that escaped the physical washing process, preventing them from entering the bloodstream. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T12#GNS212_U1_T12_h6)

question: Which nursing documentation detail is essential after finishing a gastric lavage session?

options.A: The brand name and factory serial number of the lavage tube
options.B: Total amounts of fluid put in and taken out of the stomach
options.C: The exact weight of the patient measured in kilograms
options.D: The name of the family member who gave consent for care

explanation: Recording fluid balance prevents water intoxication or electrolyte imbalances, confirming that the nurse recovered roughly what was instilled. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T12#GNS212_U1_T12_h6)

question: During a gastric lavage, a patient suddenly turns cyanotic, coughs hard, and has a drop in oxygen saturation. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Ask the patient to take deep breaths through their nose
options.B: Stop the procedure immediately and suction the airway
options.C: Instill more wash fluid to clear out any remaining blockages
options.D: Remove the protective endotracheal tube right away

explanation: These signs point to fluid aspiration into the lungs, requiring an immediate halt to fluid instillation and clearing of the airway to restore breathing. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T12#GNS212_U1_T12_h7)

question: What complication can happen if large amounts of plain tap water are used for lavage in young children?

options.A: Instant calcification of leftover food particles inside the gut
options.B: Dangerous drops in blood sodium levels known as hyponatremia
options.C: Sudden spikes in blood pressure throughout the body
options.D: Permanent hardening of the muscular walls of the stomach

explanation: Plain water lacks electrolytes, and when absorbed in large volumes across the stomach lining, it dilutes blood sodium and causes dangerous water intoxication. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T12#GNS212_U1_T12_h7)
